simple: The Avatar Context Menu, or ACM, is a small menu that pops up when a player clicks on another player's character. It has buttons to send a friend request, chat privately, view their avatar, or wave. It is off by default, so you turn it on with a LocalScript. You can also add your own buttons, like Trade or Invite to Party, remove buttons, and change its colors and fonts.
analogy: It is like tapping someone on the shoulder at a party and getting a quick list of things you can do: shake hands, chat, or swap phone numbers.
keyPoints: Turn it on with `StarterGui:SetCore("AvatarContextMenuEnabled", true)` in a LocalScript, ideally in `StarterPlayerScripts`.
It works best in games where clicking on other players does not already do something else.
Open it for a player with `SetCore("AvatarContextMenuTarget", targetPlayer)` and close it by passing `nil`.
The default buttons are Friend, Chat, View, and Wave. Players can scroll to other nearby characters in a carousel, sorted by distance.
Add a button with `SetCore("AddAvatarContextMenuOption", {"Button Name", bindableEvent})`. The event fires with the player who was clicked.
Remove a button with `SetCore("RemoveAvatarContextMenuOption", ...)` using its name or an `Enum.AvatarContextMenuOption` value.
You cannot change the menu while it is open, so check that an action still makes sense when it runs.
Change the look with `SetCore("AvatarContextMenuTheme", {...})` using settings like `BackgroundColor`, `ButtonFrameColor`, and `Font`.

terms.context menu: A small menu that shows options for the thing you clicked on.
terms.SetCore: A function on `StarterGui` that changes built-in Roblox features by name, like turning the ACM on.
terms.BindableEvent: An object that lets one script send a signal to code in the same place (client to client or server to server). Here it tells your code when your custom button is pressed.
terms.carousel: A row of choices you scroll through left and right, which loops back to the start.
terms.theme: A set of colors, fonts, and images that decide how something looks.
terms.Transparency: How see-through something is. `0` is solid, `0.5` is half see-through, and `1` is invisible.
terms.Color3: A color value. `Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 200)` is a dark blue made from red 0, green 0, and blue 200 (out of 255).
terms.programmatically: Done by a script instead of by the player clicking.

example.title: Turn on the ACM and add a custom button
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- SetCore can fail if Roblox's menus are not ready yet, so retry a few times
local function setCoreSafe(name, value)
	for attempt = 1, 10 do
		local ok = pcall(function()
			StarterGui:SetCore(name, value)
		end)
		if ok then
			return true
		end
		task.wait(1)
	end
	return false
end

-- Turn on the Avatar Context Menu
setCoreSafe("AvatarContextMenuEnabled", true)

-- Make a custom "High Five" button
local highFiveEvent = Instance.new("BindableEvent")
highFiveEvent.Event:Connect(function(targetPlayer)
	print(player.Name .. " high-fived " .. targetPlayer.Name)
end)

setCoreSafe("AddAvatarContextMenuOption", {"High Five", highFiveEvent})
explain: `setCoreSafe` tries `SetCore` and waits 1 second between tries if Roblox is not ready yet.
The first call turns the ACM on, so clicking another character opens the menu.
We make a `BindableEvent` and connect a function that runs when the button is pressed. It receives the clicked player.
`AddAvatarContextMenuOption` adds a button named "High Five" that fires our event.
To make the high five affect the server, you would fire a RemoteEvent inside that function.

watchOut: Trying to turn on the ACM from a server Script. It must be a LocalScript.
Turning on the ACM in a game where clicking players already does something, like attacking. The clicks will fight each other.
Assuming a custom action is still valid. If a Trade button is only for the market area, check both players are still there when it runs.
